reason: B is better grounded and more testable: it specifies a quenched baseline, annealing intervention, mechanical outcomes, structural characterization, and prior evidence that chemical ordering or ordered phases can impede slip and raise strength. Its main weakness is conflating true local chemical order with B2 precipitates—which must be separated experimentally to preserve the simple-solid-solution constraint—but A provides no prior evidence and an equally vague route for selectively changing short-range order.
